title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page belongs to the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' notes. M is a rank-2 projective module (or vector bundle) over a base, and rho, sigma are elements of GL(M). From earlier pages, epsilon_1 = 1 + N_1 is unipotent with N_1^2 = 0 and lies in Gamma (eq. 40 bis). Reading (56) backwards, epsilon_1 = -lambda_0 rho sigma^{-1} for a scalar lambda_0.

Step 1, eqs. (56)-(57). Conjugating by rho gives epsilon_0 = rho^{-1} epsilon_1 rho = -lambda_0 sigma^{-1} rho = 1 + N_0. Hence N_0 = rho^{-1} N_1 rho = -(lambda_0 sigma^{-1} rho + 1). Since N_0 is a conjugate of N_1, N_0^2 = 0.

Step 2, eq. (58). L_0 = {epsilon_0(lambda) = 1 + lambda N_0} is a one-parameter unipotent subgroup (a G_a) of SL(M). Its normalizer in GL(M) is called B_0. When N_0 is nowhere zero, ker N_0 = im N_0 is a line subbundle and B_0 is the Borel subgroup stabilizing it. In a basis with N_0 = E_12, B_0 consists of the upper triangular matrices (a b; 0 d).

Step 3, eqs. (59)-(60). B_0 has two characters to G_m:
- chi = det, which is ad in that basis;
- chi', defined by u N_0 u^{-1} = chi'(u) N_0, which is a/d.

Step 4, eq. (61). B~_0 is the equalizer {chi = chi'}, i.e. u N_0 u^{-1} = det(u) N_0.

Step 5, eq. (62). Grothendieck claims L_0 is contained in B~_0^* and that 1 -> L_0 -> B~_0^* -> G_m -> 1 (via det) is an exact sequence of group schemes. A marginal note says 'il faudrait le vérifier'. The asterisk on B~_0^* is added in (62) only.

Purpose. Per the previous page, B~_0^* is the scheme of matrices (mu M; 0 1), i.e. the affine group G_a ⋊ G_m. On the next page Grothendieck sets xi = [u, rho], eta = [u, sigma] for u in B~_0^* and wants to show they automatically satisfy the loop-type relation xi = eta epsilon_1(mu - 1) with mu = det u. He first checks this for u in L_0, using sigma epsilon_0 sigma^{-1} = rho epsilon_0 rho^{-1} = epsilon_1. So this page sets up a group-scheme parametrization of a family of solutions of the loop equation in GL_2 by the affine group normalizing a unipotent line.
errors: As literally defined in (61), B~_0 is the locus ad = a/d, i.e. d^2 = 1. Its kernel under det is mu_2·L_0 (in char ≠ 2 it contains the matrices (-1 b; 0 -1)), not L_0. So 1 -> L_0 -> B~_0 -> G_m -> 1 is not exact for B~_0 itself. One must pass to the subgroup with d = 1, i.e. the subgroup acting trivially on M/ker N_0 (the affine group (mu M; 0 1)). The asterisk in B~_0^* and the marginal 'il faudrait le vérifier' suggest Grothendieck noticed this.
Over a general base, the normalizer of L_0 is a Borel only where N_0 is nowhere vanishing (so that im N_0 is a line subbundle). This hypothesis is implicit.

ideas.what: Conjugating the unipotent epsilon_1 to epsilon_0 = 1 + N_0 with N_0^2 = 0, and taking the one-parameter subgroup lambda -> 1 + lambda N_0 in SL(M)
ideas.modern_name: unipotent one-parameter subgroup G_a in SL_2 (root group)
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 (root data, Borel subgroups of reductive group schemes)

ideas.what: Normalizer of the root group as a Borel subgroup; character chi' giving the action on Lie(L_0); the subgroup where chi' = det; exact sequence 1 -> G_a -> affine group -> G_m -> 1
ideas.modern_name: Borel subgroup, root character, affine group Aff_1 = G_a ⋊ G_m

ideas.what: Using commutators [u, rho], [u, sigma] with u in the affine group to generate solutions of the 'équation des lacets' (continued on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: parametrizing a component of a rank-2 representation/solution scheme by an orbit of a solvable group

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine linear algebra and group-scheme bookkeeping (root group, Borel normalizer, characters, affine group) inside a longer computation of rank-2 solutions of the loop equation. The only notable point is a small exactness slip that Grothendieck himself flagged.
transcription_corrections: Line 'dont le normalisateur dans GL(M)': the manuscript shows a bold G(M) (written over) where GL(M) is meant, and 'SL(M)' looks written as 'SG(M)'.
In (61) the asterisk is not present; it appears only in (62) as B~_0^* (with a superscript tilde/star). In the exact sequence the middle term is also written B~_0 with tilde, over 'det'.
In (58) a small 'epsilon_0' label precedes the map lambda -> epsilon_0(lambda); fine as transcribed.
Bottom margin reads roughly 'il faudrait le vérifier ... je pense'; it is a doubt about (62).
Left oblique margin note is mostly illegible; it mentions gamma, u and 'coefficients de (r s; x u)'.
